align.prompt: Run the LLM straighten ablation baseline for as-twn-taipei on the orig-llm-skeleton2grid-fable5 flow (forced re-run from scratch), then chain into the LLM network loop.

transcript.note: Round 1 — lock-table sweep. I first built a per-vertex lock table from hvSegs (a V segment pins the vertex's col, an H segment pins its row) and only moved vertices along their free axis, so all 47 existing H/V segments are preserved by construction. Within that constraint I worked the 27 offSegs by degree: (a) free leaf/degree-2 vertices got pulled onto their neighbour's row or col — 43->(4,17) squares 33-43 onto row 17, 42->(9,20) and 39->(12,20) put 39-42 on row 20, 1->(11,3) with 3->(14,3) makes 3-1 horizontal while turning 2-3 into a clean 45 diagonal, 4->(6,3) plus 47->(2,3) turns the northwest stub into a V+H elbow, 29->(6,27) and 50->(7,30) do the same on the southwest branch, 28->(7,25) drops onto col 7 to make 28-51 vertical, 0->(12,10) makes 20-0 vertical; (b) hubs were moved only where the incident bearing cycle is provably unchanged — 44->(16,17) collects three edges at once (36-44 and 44-40 become horizontal, 44-58 becomes a 45 diagonal) and its col-16 pins survive, 18->(13,13) makes 18-20 horizontal and I checked the atan2 cycles of both 18 and 20 are identical before and after, 55->(23,17) makes 34-55 horizontal and keeps 55-32 vertical. (c) 38 is fully free but its two diagonal neighbours 23 and 12 sit on the SAME row 16, so the tempting (17,16) would land the vertex on top of the existing 23-12 segment; I took (18,15) instead, which makes 38-12 vertical and lines 38-12-40 into one straight col-18 run at the cost of the 38-23 diagonal — H/V is the primary key so that trade is worth it. 35->(6,11) keeps the 4-35 column vertical while turning 35-45 into a 45 diagonal.

Round 2 — upgrade the 45 diagonals to true H/V, since HV is the primary key and a diagonal already counts in HVD (so the upgrade is free on the secondary key). Three of the four remaining diagonals can be closed: 35->(6,13) slides down its own free axis (col 6 is pinned by 4-35, the row is free) and makes 35-45 horizontal, which also welds 35-45-20-18 into one straight row-13 run; 16->(12,19) puts 16 on 39's column so 16-39 becomes vertical, and I verified 16's four-way bearing cycle (33,58,39,15) and 39's three-way cycle (16,25,42) are both unchanged. 2-3 needs a shared column but the two ends are 4 cells apart, over the short-move budget, so I split it symmetrically: 2->(16,7) and 3->(16,3), two cells each, meeting at col 16 — 2 keeps its row-7 pin from 13-2 and 3 keeps its row-3 pin from 3-1, so nothing is spent. The fourth diagonal 44-58 is unreachable: both ends are pinned on both axes (44 by 44-23/44-24 vertically and 36-44/44-40 horizontally, 58 by 36-58 and 58-24/58-16). The nine genuinely unaligned segments left (45-36, 36-23, 13-38, 38-23, 38-18, 23-20, 16-15, 16-33, 2-18) all run between vertices that are pinned on both axes, or whose only aligning target would land a vertex on top of an existing segment — e.g. 16 onto col 8 would sit inside 15-33, and 20 onto col 16 would make 45-20 swallow 18. Those are structural, not budget, limits.

Round 3 — the last free axis on the board. I re-derived the lock table and of the 13 endpoints touching an unaligned segment, twelve are now pinned on BOTH axes (several doubly: 44 is held by 44-23 and 44-24 vertically and by 36-44 and 44-40 horizontally). Only vertex 38 still has a free row. Sliding it two cells down to (18,13) puts it on 18's row, so 38-18 becomes a clean horizontal run c=13..18, while its col-18 pin from 38-12 is untouched and 13-38 / 38-23 stay unaligned but no worse. I checked the two things that could bite: (a) the winding cycle at 38 is 18,13,12,23 before and after, and at 18 it is 37,2,38,20 before and after; (b) the new row-13 span c=13..18 is clear — the other row-13 occupants (35, 45, 20, 18) all sit at c<=13, and the col-18 traffic (40-12, 40-10, 10-9) all sits at r>=16, so nothing gets swallowed. The other nine unaligned segments cannot be improved without a net-negative trade: every candidate either breaks one H/V to buy one back (23->col 15, 36->row 16, 13->col 18, 18->row 7, 16->row 17 are all exactly net zero) or breaks two to buy one (20->row 16, 45 off row 13). H/V being the primary key, none of those are worth taking, so this is the stopping point.
